newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Adgas in LNG supply talks to Korea Gas - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Adgas in LNG supply talks to Korea Gas - MEES.

text.p: Abu Dhabi Gas Liquefaction Co (Adgas) is in talks with Korea Gas Corp to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) after Adgas's main client cut liftings, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"Volume and pricing negotiations between Adgas and Korea Gas ...are believed to center around around the Korean firm taking four cargoes totaling some 250,000 tonnes in 1997, rising to 750,000 tonnes in 1998, 1.2 million tonnes in 1999 and 750,000 tonnes in 2000," the Cyprus-based MEES reported.

KOGAS was interested in supplies from Abu Dhabi to cover short-falls in contracts from Malaysia and Indonesia between 1997-1999 and before the start of contracts from Qatar in 1999 and Oman in the year 2000.
Adgas's main customer, Japan's Tokyo Electric Power Company (Tepco), cut its contract from March to April 1998 to 4.45 million tonnes from 4.7 million tonnes.
"The volume reduction for fiscal 1997 is understood to be a one-off arrangement and Tepco's purchase obligations in fiscal year 1997 is understood to be a one-off arrangement," MEES said.
Adgas also has a supply contract with Spain's Enagas and sells cargoes on the spot market.
